observations.notes: Claims of motive, treachery or military causation remain the paper’s accusations.

observations.description: An address to friends in Great Britain and Ireland seeks continued organizing and funds, and describes assistance with food, shelter, advice and employment for people arriving from slavery.
observations.attribution: The named paper/document makes this argument or prints this report; no independent validation of its allegations is implied.
observations.notes: A named overseas appeal is evidence of an intended relationship, not a count of readers, donors or people persuaded.

observations.description: Lincoln’s reply to Greeley distinguishes his stated official aim of saving the Union from his personal wish for universal freedom.

observations.notes: The reply says it answers Greeley’s letter of the 19th through the Tribune. The original letter’s full text and its readership are not reconstructed from the answer.

observations.notes: Printing on this issue date does not date receipt by every subscriber.

observations.description: Drafting—What Is the Duty of the Abolitionists? distinguishes individual decisions from a uniform abolitionist exemption or a single compulsory response.

observations.notes: The argument acknowledges differing convictions; it is not a universal abolitionist voting or enlistment rate.

observations.notes: [I] Five calendar days separate the named publication dates; this is not an observed mail-transit time or a general delivery coefficient.

observations.description: Hudson’s later account credits the Herald with organizing army/navy correspondents and maintaining a Southern-paper bureau as the war began.

rules: Editorial claims, document publication and actual receipt are distinct.
